kind: Positive exponential endpoints and greatest right limits
scope: A common continuous upper barrier for every genuine subsolution at exponents bounded away from zero gives a logarithmically corrected order for greatest solutions. A positive solvable endpoint is admitted exactly when some exact solution sequence has bounded-below suprema; an excluded positive endpoint forces every exact sequence to lose mass. At every admitted positive exponent, greatest solutions converge from the right in L1 and capacity, with total-variation convergence of equation measures. Intrinsic density criteria, actual excluded-endpoint examples and left continuity remain undecided.

direct_analytic_review_obligations.fixed-setting: Connected compact Hermitian X, fixed positive smooth volume, nonzero nonnegative L1 density; all limits use the same f.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.greatest-selection: At every admitted exponent an exact solution is a subsolution, so the retained theorem supplies a greatest solution dominating every genuine subsolution.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.upper-interval-premise: The retained upper-interval proposition implies every exponent above the finite infimum of a nonempty set is admitted.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.uniform-barrier-parameter: The parameter tau is any strictly positive number, whether or not tau belongs to the admitted set.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.bounded-truncation: q=min(f,1) is bounded, nonnegative and nonzero, hence in every finite Lp on compact X.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.Nguyen-premises: The bounded nonzero density and positive tau satisfy the retained continuous exponential-solvability theorem.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.upward-translation: t=w+max(0,-inf w) is continuous h-psh, nonnegative and has the same Monge-Ampere measure as w.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.supersolution-direction: w<=t and t>=0 imply exp(tau w)q<=exp(tau t)f<=exp(lambda t)f for lambda>=tau.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.strict-set-factor: On t<u-epsilon, exp(lambda t)f<=exp(-lambda epsilon)exp(lambda u)f; the subsolution inequality gives the strict domination hypothesis.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.domination-background: Hermitian h is semipositive and big, as required by the retained singular strict-domination theorem.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.smaller-envelope: The constant inf t is a competitor for P_(h/2)(t), so this envelope is genuine.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.singularity-order: Every genuine quasi-psh u has finite supremum while t is bounded below, yielding u-epsilon<=t+C and hence u-epsilon precedes t.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.strict-constant: For positive lambda and epsilon, exp(-lambda epsilon)<1; domination gives t>=u-epsilon and passage epsilon->0 gives the upper bound.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.upper-bound-sign: K=sup t is finite and nonnegative; the sign is retained in every exponent and logarithmic estimate.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.shifted-order: delta=K(lambda2-lambda1)/lambda2 is nonnegative and finite. Since U_lambda1<=K, lambda2(U_lambda1-delta)<=lambda1 U_lambda1.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.cross-exponent-subsolution: Constant invariance and the previous scalar inequality make U_lambda1-delta a genuine subsolution at lambda2; no potential scaling is used.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.greatest-order: Maximality of the greatest subsolution supplies U_lambda2>=U_lambda1-delta without a singular comparison between the two unbounded solutions.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.logarithmic-inequality: For x>=1, log x>=1-1/x, since their difference vanishes at 1 and has derivative (x-1)/x^2>=0.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.corrected-direction: Adding K log(lambda/tau) makes the greatest family nondecreasing as lambda increases; it therefore decreases along lambda_j downarrow a.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.positive-endpoint: For nonempty Lambda with infimum a>0, a is finite and all lambda>a are admitted. Zero is not treated as a positive endpoint.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.attained-lower-barrier: An exact solution u_a shifted downward to s<=0 is a genuine subsolution at every lambda>=a. The greatest family dominates this same s.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.endpoint-sequence: Choose lambda_j=a+1/j and the greatest solutions; their suprema are bounded below by sup s.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.common-upper-for-arbitrary-solutions: The uniform barrier applies to any exact solution, not just the greatest family.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.finite-suprema-subsequence: The hypothesized lower bound and K_a give a compact real interval for sup u_j, so a subsequence has finite limit M.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.normalized-compactness: Normalized u_j-sup u_j have a genuine h-psh L1 cluster v; adding the finite scalar limit gives genuine L1 limit u.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.almost-everywhere-extraction: L1 convergence admits a further dV-almost-everywhere convergent subsequence; genuine potentials are finite dV-almost everywhere.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.density-domination: lambda_j<=lambda1, u_j<=K_a and K_a>=0 bound all exponential densities by exp(lambda1 K_a)f.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.density-L1-limit: At finite almost-everywhere points lambda_j u_j->a u; dominated convergence identifies the L1 density limit exp(a u)f.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.lower-density-closure: The retained closure lemma uses common upper bound, genuine L1 potential limit and L1 density convergence to give only MA(u)>=exp(a u)f.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.endpoint-exact-existence: A genuine endpoint subsolution yields an exact greatest solution by the retained theorem; no equality of MA(u) is inferred directly from L1 compactness.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.excluded-endpoint-escape: Failure of sup u_j->-infinity would yield a subsequence with uniformly bounded-below suprema and contradict the endpoint criterion.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.positive-exponent-collapse: Once sup u_j<0, lambda_j>=a>0 gives exp(lambda_j u_j)<=exp(a sup u_j)->0, including value zero at poles.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.excluded-endpoint-mass: Exact nonnegative finite mass is at most exp(a sup u_j)||f||1, so it converges to zero without a total-mass order assumption.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.admitted-right-lower-bound: For a admitted and K=K_a, corrected V_j lie above U_a by the logarithmic order estimate including lambda1=a.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.genuine-monotone-limit: Decreasing h-psh V_j have genuine lower bound U_a and integrable upper bound V1, so their limit is genuine.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.L1-monotone-limit: Dominated convergence between the integrable bounds gives L1 convergence, independently of the capacity lemma.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.capacity-monotone-limit: The retained monotone-potential capacity lemma applies to the genuine decreasing limit. Constants K log(lambda_j/a)->0 preserve L1 and capacity convergence.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.nonpositive-translation: U_lambda_j-K<=0, and the limiting V-K is nonpositive; constant invariance preserves the equation measures.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.positive-closedness-premises: The exponent limit a is positive; exp(lambda_j K)f->exp(aK)f in L1; dV is finite and non-pluripolar; capacity convergence was already proved.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.exact-right-limit: The retained exponential-closedness theorem gives MA(V)=exp(aV)f and total-variation convergence. Greatest maximality and V>=U_a force equality of potentials.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.full-right-parameter-limit: Every decreasing sequence gives the same limit; a failure of the full right limit would have a decreasing bad subsequence.
direct_analytic_review_obligations.scope-boundaries: Only greatest solutions are claimed to converge at admitted positive exponents. Intrinsic density criteria, actual excluded-endpoint examples, left continuity and arbitrary singularity-type solution limits remain undecided.
